about: Where `$$` display maths opens and closes, read the same on the phone (apps/mobile/lib/markdown/displayDollars.ts) and on the server (apps/api/app/modules/chat/display_dollars.py). remark-math's rule: a delimiter is a run of exactly two unescaped dollars (three or more, or one in brackets, is a price tier); at the start of a line (after its indent, a quote mark or a list marker) it opens a formula that may run on over the lines below; mid-line it is maths as $$x$$ with nothing between the dollars and the formula, closed on its line, or as a $$ that ends a sentence's line, closed by a $$ that starts a line before a blank line; a $$ alone on its line, or with TeX after it, opens a block only its closer ends (a line inside it like |x| < 5 or - 3x &= 2 is maths), while one with words after it or in a list item reads as prose, which a list item or table row ends unclosed; a pair on a table row never spans a |. Inline code holds no maths. `display` lists each formula's text between its dollars, trimmed, in order. The phone's tests (lib/__tests__/displayDollars.test.ts) read every case with the reader, convertBlockMath and the streaming scanners; the server's (app/tests/modules/chat/test_display_dollars.py) with its reader, display_math_lines and the LaTeX check.
